Released: 10 August 2026

WEM 1.3.0 includes new features, enhancements, and bug fixes.

## Highlights

- **Host agent:** WEM 1.3 provides a new `acp-host-agent` package, a separate service that runs on the WarehousePG coordinator host and executes privileged operations on behalf of WEM. The host agent connects to WEM's internal job-execution engine, which makes operations reliable and recoverable even when connectivity is interrupted. See [Installing the host agent](../installing/host-agent).
- **Bundled Alertmanager:** WEM now runs Alertmanager as an internal managed subprocess rather than requiring a separately installed and configured instance. See [Configuring WEM](../installing/wem).
- **Fully agent-based HBA editor:** The HBA editor now operates through the host agent regardless of whether WEM is installed on the same host as the WarehousePG coordinator. See [Modifying authentication rules](../system-access/access-management#modifying-authentication-rules).

## Features

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Alert rule configuration</summary><hr/><p>Previously, creating or editing an alert rule meant editing a Prometheus rule YAML file directly. In 1.3, the <strong>Rules</strong> tab in the <strong>Alerts</strong> panel lets you create and edit rules through a builder (metric, comparison operator, threshold, and label filters), or as raw PromQL. Built-in system rules can't be deleted by anyone, including Admins. Admins can edit or delete any user-created rule, but Operators can only manage their own. The <strong>Notifications</strong> tab now lets you edit the Alertmanager configuration file directly to set up Slack, email, or other receivers. The <strong>History</strong> tab adds a rule-name filter and an Admin-only option to delete history, either entirely or by date range. See <a href="../monitoring/alerts">Managing alerts</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>System Metrics improvements</summary><hr/><p>The <strong>System Metrics</strong> views now support filtering by individual node, so you can isolate CPU, memory, and disk usage for a specific host. Time-range controls are also refactored, and charts adapt their formatting to the selected time span. See <a href="../monitoring/system-metrics">Visualizing hardware performance</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Data Analysis improvements</summary><hr/><p>WEM now uses dedicated database views to compute object sizes, replacing per-object size queries and reducing overhead when browsing large schemas. On WHPG 7 clusters, Admins can also switch skew calculations from a fast catalog-based estimate to an accurate mode that scans the file system for exact figures. See <a href="../performance/data-analysis">Analyzing data distribution</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Query Monitor improvements</summary><hr/><p>A new chart on the <strong>Longest Queries</strong> tab shows the top 50 longest-running queries over time, making it easier to spot and investigate persistent slow queries. A new <strong>Historical Queries</strong> tab shows completed queries along with a cumulative query count. See <a href="../performance/query-monitor#identifying-the-longest-running-queries">Identifying the longest-running queries</a> and <a href="../performance/query-monitor">Monitoring and evaluating queries</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Log viewer improvements</summary><hr/><p>Log views now display the <strong>User</strong> and <strong>Source Host</strong> for each log entry, making it easier to trace activity back to a specific database user or client machine. The log viewer also supports fetching all matching records through server-side pagination, with a live progress counter and the option to cancel a long-running fetch, and exported CSV files match exactly what's shown in the grid. See <a href="../monitoring/logs">Auditing system logs</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Password reset links and CLI command</summary><hr/><p>Admins can generate single-use password reset links for users from the <strong>Management</strong> panel. A new <code>wem reset-password</code> CLI command supports local or offline password resets and automatically loads <code>wem.conf</code> in standard installations. See <a href="../system-access/management">Performing administrative management</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>pg_hba.conf tab improvements</summary><hr/><p>The <strong>pg_hba.conf</strong> tab in <strong>Access Management</strong> distinguishes cluster-internal trust rules from broad-network trust rules, making it easier to spot overly permissive entries. Saving changes also now propagates the update to the standby coordinator automatically, keeping both coordinators consistent. See <a href="../system-access/access-management#modifying-authentication-rules">Modifying authentication rules</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Storage date range picker</summary><hr/><p>The <strong>Storage &gt; Historical</strong> tab now includes a date range picker for precise control over the time window for storage trend analysis. See <a href="../performance/storage">Planning storage capacity</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Changes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Alertmanager configuration</summary><hr/><p>The <code>ALERTMANAGER_URL</code> and <code>CONFIG_PATH</code> configuration parameters are removed, since Alertmanager is now bundled and requires no external URL. If you're upgrading, remove these from your existing <code>wem.conf</code>. See <a href="../installing/upgrading">Upgrading WarehousePG Enterprise Manager</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Canary Checks panel</summary><hr/><p>The <strong>Monitoring</strong> panel is renamed to <strong>Canary Checks</strong>. Configuration of these checks, previously Admin-only in the <strong>Management</strong> panel, is now consolidated here. Operators and Viewers can view results. Admins can create, edit, and delete checks. See <a href="../monitoring/monitoring">Validating database responsiveness</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Longest Queries performance</summary><hr/><p>WEM now caches longest-running query data from the external table on a background schedule instead of scanning it on every request, cutting typical lookup times from tens of seconds to milliseconds. See <a href="../performance/query-monitor#identifying-the-longest-running-queries">Identifying the longest-running queries</a>.</p>
</details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>


## Bug Fixes

<table class="table w-100"><thead><tr><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed the dashboard failing silently when <code>WEM_COOKIE_SECRET</code> is unset.</summary><hr/><p>WEM now validates the cookie secret at startup and surfaces a clear error.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed host agent installation to handle local authentication scenarios for the configuration database connection, and to work with new installation paths.</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed issues editing and saving the Alertmanager configuration file.</summary><hr/><p>Changes that fail to reload now roll back automatically, so the saved file always matches the running instance.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed timeouts on Data Analysis skew and top-tables queries on large clusters.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed a race condition where saving pg_hba.conf to the standby coordinator returned success before the operation finished.</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed the canary trend chart showing an incorrect Y-axis scale.</summary><hr/><p>The chart now correctly shows a weighted success ratio.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed pagination behavior across UI tables</summary><hr/><p>Pagination now resets correctly when filters change, and page controls are consistent across all views.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed the pg_hba.conf tab to match the backend's trust-rule classification, and to refresh HBA statistics immediately after saving.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed table size and compression estimates in Data Analysis to compute from catalog metadata, improving accuracy and performance on large schemas.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed alert history and the users audit log to no longer cap results at 500 rows.</td></tr>
<tr><td><details><summary>Fixed the partition details view</summary><hr/><p>The partition details view no longer caps results at 500 rows, shows the immediate parent table instead of the root table for multi-level partitions, and correctly counts partitions and indexes across all levels.</p>
</details></td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed the database size collector to run in the background instead of blocking the request that triggers it.</td></tr>
<tr><td>Fixed user creation to correctly apply the Active status from the request.</td></tr>
</tbody></table>
